deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Π = Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞}. It is free profinite on two generators, with inertia generators ℓ_0, ℓ_1, ℓ_∞ satisfying one product relation. The convention used here appears to be ℓ_∞ ℓ_1 ℓ_0 = 1, since relation (1) is the image of this relation under u. The page uses two symmetries from the S_3 acting on {0,1,∞}:
- σ_0 is an involution fixing 0 and swapping 1 and ∞, so σ_0(ℓ_1) = ℓ_∞. This is forced by the NB computation h_1' = ℓ_∞^{-μ} h_1 ℓ_1^{μ}. Concretely σ_0 is z ↦ z/(z−1).
- ρ is the 3-cycle, presumably ℓ_0 → ℓ_1 → ℓ_∞ → ℓ_0 up to conjugation.

Problem. Describe the automorphisms u of Π that commute with σ_0 (modulo inner automorphisms) and commute with ρ in Out(Π). In modern terms: elements of Aut/Out(F̂_2) that commute with the S_3-symmetry. This is the 'level 0' part of what became the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group: the 2-cycle and 3-cycle (hexagon) relations, without the pentagon.

Parametrization. Write u(ℓ_1) = int(g_1) ℓ_1^p and u(ℓ_∞) = int(g_∞) ℓ_∞^p, with p ∈ Ẑ^* (the cyclotomic character / λ) and g_1 well defined modulo ℓ_1^{Ẑ}. Commuting with σ_0 forces g_∞ = σ_0(g_1). Put h_1 = σ_0(g_1)^{-1} g_1. Conjugating u by g_∞^{-1} gives the normal form:
- ℓ_∞ ↦ ℓ_∞^p,
- ℓ_1 ↦ h_1 ℓ_1^p h_1^{-1}.
Here h_1 plays the role of Drinfeld's f(x,y). Since σ_0 is an involution, σ_0(h_1) = g_1^{-1} σ_0(g_1) = h_1^{-1}. So Drinfeld's 2-cycle relation f(x,y) f(y,x) = 1 is built into the parametrization rather than imposed.

The ρ-condition. Exterior commutation with ρ determines u(ℓ_0) = int(g_0) ℓ_0^p, with g_0 = g_1 ℓ_1^{-γ} ρ^{-1}(h_1) (margin NB). This requires relation (2): ρ(h_1) ℓ_∞^{-γ} h_1 ℓ_1^{-γ} ρ^{-1}(h_1) = ℓ_0^β. The exponents β, γ ∈ Ẑ are unique because the centralizer of an inertia generator in the free profinite group is pro-cyclic.

The product relation. u must preserve ℓ_∞ ℓ_1 ℓ_0 = 1. After normalizing by g_∞^{-1} this is relation (1): ℓ_∞^p · int(h_1)(ℓ_1^p) · int(h_1 ℓ_1^{-γ} ρ^{-1}(h_1))(ℓ_0^p) = 1. Substituting (2) gives (1'): ℓ_∞^p · int(h_1)(ℓ_1^p) · int(ℓ_∞^γ ρ(h_1)^{-1})(ℓ_0^p) = 1. Unwound, this is a cyclic product of three conjugated powers. It is the analogue of the 3-cycle relation f(z,x) z^m f(y,z) y^m f(x,y) x^m = 1, with γ (and β) playing the role of m = (λ−1)/2.

Final NB (gauge ambiguity). Replacing g_1 by g_1 ℓ_1^μ changes h_1 to ℓ_∞^{-μ} h_1 ℓ_1^{μ}. Relation (1') then transforms by int(ℓ_∞^{-μ}), and β, γ are unchanged. This is exactly the ambiguity that Drinfeld/Ihara later remove by requiring f to lie in the commutator subgroup F̂_2'.

Context. The previous page studies commensurator-type groups H of a lattice π acting on the universal cover. The next page studies automorphisms compatible with a quotient π → π' and with extensions S(π). So this page is a computation inside Grothendieck's 1981 program on the Galois/Teichmüller action on π_1 of moduli spaces (Longue Marche period).
errors: Minor apparent slip in the last displayed formula: it is transcribed as int(ℓ_∞^γ ρ^{-1}(h_1')^{-1}) but should read int(ℓ_∞^γ ρ(h_1')^{-1}) to match (1'). It may be a transcription or handwriting issue.

Relation (2) is described as a condition in which β, γ exist and are unique, but existence of β, γ is part of the hypothesis; the page does not discuss which p, g_1 admit them. This is a gap in exposition, not an error.

The order of the product relation (ℓ_∞ℓ_1ℓ_0 = 1) and the precise direction of ρ are not stated on the page. The consistency of (1) with u(ℓ_0) depends on these conventions; they check out under ℓ_∞ℓ_1ℓ_0 = 1 and σ_0(ℓ_1) = ℓ_∞.
The margin NB ('On doit avoir ρ^μ σ_0 ...') is illegible and its content cannot be verified.

ideas.what: Description of automorphisms of the profinite π_1 of P^1−{0,1,∞} commuting (outer) with the S_3 symmetries, parametrized by p ∈ Ẑ^* and an element h_1 ∈ F̂_2.
ideas.modern_name: Pair (λ, f) of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT̂ (or its 'level 0' part without the pentagon); Ihara's description of the Galois image in Out(F̂_2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for GT̂; Ihara (1985–1990) for the Galois-side relations; Grothendieck's Esquisse (1984) for the program
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) describes the Teichmüller tower and S_3-symmetry heuristically but gives no explicit relations; unsure whether La Longue Marche (1981) contains equivalent formulas

ideas.what: Parametrizing via g_1 and g_∞ = σ_0(g_1), so that h_1 = σ_0(g_1)^{-1}g_1 automatically satisfies σ_0(h_1) = h_1^{-1}.
Relations (2) and (1'): exterior ρ-equivariance plus the product relation give a cyclic product of conjugated powers with exponent shifts β, γ.
Gauge freedom g_1 ↦ g_1ℓ_1^μ, under which β and γ are invariant.
ideas.modern_name: Normalization f ∈ F̂_2' (commutator subgroup) in the definition of GT̂

missed.claim: In spring 1981 Grothendieck explicitly computed the conditions on an automorphism of Π̂_{0,3} commuting with σ_0 and exteriorly with ρ. The result is the 2-cycle relation, built in through g_∞ = σ_0(g_1), and a 3-cycle/hexagon-type relation (1') with exponent shifts β, γ. This predates Ihara's explicit relations (mid-1980s) and Drinfeld's GT̂ (1990). The published Esquisse contains only the heuristic program.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: it documents that the two 'level 0' GT relations were in Grothendieck's hands in 1981 in explicit form, a nontrivial piece of the prehistory of GT̂. The σ_0-equivariant parametrization making the 2-cycle relation automatic is a pleasant presentation choice.

missed.claim: The pentagon (level-1, Π̂_{0,5}) condition is absent here. The page does not determine which (p, g_1) actually admit β, γ, nor how β, γ relate to p. In GT the analogous exponent is m = (λ−1)/2, determined by abelianization.
missed.quote: β, γ ∈ Ẑ sont uniquement déterminés par g_1, p
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly superseded by the GT literature. It might interest someone comparing the 'S_3-only' group GT_0 with GT̂.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is now standard GT theory, but seeing Grothendieck in 1981 derive explicit 2-cycle and hexagon-type relations, with the gauge ambiguity noted, is a notable unpublished detail. It predates Ihara and Drinfeld. That Grothendieck worked on this is broadly known, but the explicit formulas are not in his published texts.
transcription_corrections: Final formula: 'int([-…-]ℓ_∞^γ ρ^{-1}(h_1')^{-1})' should likely be 'int(ℓ_∞^γ ρ(h_1')^{-1})', matching (1').
The interlinear insertion in the first line, transcribed '{+intérieurs[?]+}', is doubtful; the sense ('automorphismes ... commutant extérieurement à ρ') suggests it is not 'intérieurs'.
Margin note 'NB On a donc u(ℓ_0) = int(g_1 ℓ_1^{-γ} ρ^{-1}(h_1)) ℓ_0^p' with the underbrace labelled g_0: this is consistent with the main text.
